subject: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment qualification - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Ellis <john.ellis@legacybank.com>, Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@legacybank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 14:10:00 -07:00
Subject: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment qualification - follow up & next steps

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet you both. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the on-prem / air-gapped requirements we discussed: 

1) High-level goal
- LegacyBank wants a private, air-gapped deployment of Redwood to run inference for customer-facing workflows with strict network restrictions and quarterly maintenance windows.

2) Items we need from your side (action items)
- Hardware inventory (make/model, CPU, RAM, GPU type & counts, storage layout) — helps us size Dedicated vs full Private on-prem.
- Confirmation on upgrade process constraints (can you accept USB/image-based upgrades delivered during a maintenance window? any signed-for update process?)
- Preferred maintenance windows and blackout periods.
- Network diagram and allowed egress list (if any) — even with air-gapped setups we often need details for administrative access and licensing.
- Primary infra POC for on-site coordination (name, phone, best times).

3) Redwood next steps
- I’ll loop in Rishi (solutions engineering) to prepare an offline-upgrade ops plan and a baseline on-prem checklist.
- We’ll propose two workshop dates (one remote technical deep-dive, one on-site hardware workshop) once we have the inventory.

Attachments: I’ve attached our standard on-prem checklist (draft) — it's a short workbook to capture the inventory and common constraints. Please fill what you can and send the hardware inventory export if available.

If it helps, suggested first-step: export a CSV from your CMDB with the above hardware columns and share it. Happy to take raw output and clean it up.

Availability: I’m available Wed/Fri next week for a 60-min technical deep-dive.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive\Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_onprem_checklist.xlsx]

From: John Ellis <john.ellis@legacybank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@legacybank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment qualification - follow up & next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear list. Answers inline below.

> Hardware inventory (make/model, CPU, RAM, GPU type & counts, storage layout)
We attached a CSV export from our asset management tool (hardware_inventory.csv). Brief summary: two racks in DC-2, each rack has 4 HPE DL380 Gen11 nodes with dual-socket AMD Milan CPUs, 1TB RAM per node, and an NVIDIA A100 80GB (PCIe) per node. Storage is local NVMe + replicated NAS for archives. We also have 2 spare nodes in a cold cabinet for N+1.

> Upgrade process constraints (USB/image-based upgrades)
We are air-gapped for production cluster. We can accept signed, checksum-verified images on encrypted USB drives during scheduled maintenance windows. Any automated outbound license checks are blocked; we need self-contained upgrade packages.

> Preferred maintenance windows and blackout periods
Primary window: Saturday 02:00–06:00 local (ET). No changes allowed last-week-of-quarter.

> Network diagram / allowed egress
Attached is our network summary (legacybank_network_requirements.pdf). For production, egress is blocked; management VLANs can reach an internal patching server.

> Primary infra POC
- Sarah Nguyen, Lead Systems Engineer — sarah.nguyen@legacybank.com, +1 415-555-0192 (best after 09:30 PT).

We’re open to an on-site workshop; please propose dates. Also: do you have any special requirements for the USB staging images (signed artifacts, signature scheme)?

Regards,
John Ellis
Director, Infrastructure\LegacyBank
[Attachment: legacybank_network_requirements.pdf]
[Attachment: hardware_inventory.csv]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Ellis <john.ellis@legacybank.com>, Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@legacybank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment qualification - follow up & next steps

Fantastic — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments, that helps a lot. A few clarifications and proposed next steps: 

- USB staging & signing: we support producing signed image artifacts (SHA256 + PGP signature). We’ll deliver an encrypted archive with a detached signature and an instruction checklist for verification. Is PGP acceptable, or do you prefer another signature method?

- Maintenance windows: Saturday 02:00–06:00 ET works for us. We’ll plan upgrades as offline bundles staged onto a USB and validated by your team during that window.

- N+1: good to hear you have spares — that fits our recommendations for high-availability. We’ll document recommended failover steps for node replacement in the ops playbook.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Rishi will draft an offline-upgrade ops plan and an acceptance-test checklist for the initial deployment.
2) Schedule a remote 60-min technical deep-dive (I’m proposing Wed 18 Nov at 10:00 PT or Fri 20 Nov at 11:00 PT).
3) After the deep-dive, plan a 1-day on-site workshop focused on hardware staging and initial install (we can align calendars after the deep-dive).

Can you confirm which of the two deep-dive slots works best for Sarah / infra team? Also confirm PGP signing is fine and we’ll produce the first-stage image artifacts accordingly.

Thanks — looping in Rishi for the ops plan (cc’d).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive\Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_onprem_checklist.xlsx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: LegacyBank on-prem follow-up / action items

Quick internal note and ask — summarizing the external thread so we’re aligned before the deep-dive: 

- External context: LegacyBank confirmed DC hardware (HPE DL380 Gen11, A100 80GB), air-gapped production, USB-staged upgrades, maintenance window Saturdays 02:00–06:00 ET, contact Sarah Nguyen.

Action items:
- Rishi: please draft the offline-upgrade ops plan and acceptance-test checklist. Key items: image signing verification steps, rollback plan, node replacement steps, QA checks (latency, throughput, KV cache integrity), and recommended snapshot cadence. Please have a first draft by EOD Wed 18 Nov.
- Vivek: provide initial throughput and memory/quantization recommendations for A100 80GB nodes (expected QPS target: 30 qps steady, 120 qps burst) — include suggestions for batching, KV cache sizing, and any recommended fp16/4-bit quant profiles for balance between latency and cost. Deliver by EOD Thu 19 Nov.
- Marissa: I’ll coordinate deep-dive scheduling and update the HubSpot deal with attachments and next steps.

Flagging risk: we should verify whether their NAS replication policy will interfere with our local model checkpoints (I/O patterns). Rishi — please include a short I/O checklist to share with Sarah in the workshop.

Thanks — I’ll schedule the deep-dive pending Sarah’s slot confirmation.

Marissa
Senior Account Executive\Redwood Inference
